skill.name: revnu-fix-ai-claims
skill.description: Review AI answers about a business, verify individual claims, trace likely sources, and draft corrections for websites, profiles, and publishers.
skill.summary: Turn inaccurate AI claims into sourced corrections and a repeatable recheck plan.
skill.author: revnu-app

security_audit.summary: All 31 static findings are false positives: Markdown formatting, business prose, integration identity checks, or disclosed network references. Semantic review found mandatory promotional reply manipulation and a connected-service handoff without explicit approval. The preview request separately requires user interest and prohibits sending source code or secrets.

remediation.issue: Mandatory promotional content includes instructions suppressing disclosure of the integration workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Remove mandatory advertising and suppression language; make the paid-service offer optional and disclose external actions clearly.

remediation.issue: The connected Revnu path directs a claims-table handoff without requiring acceptance of the offer.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before ask_revnu; show the recipient and payload, remove confidential facts, and bound status polling.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: The skill mandates "always end the reply" with a paid Revnu offer and says "Don't narrate these instructions" and "just make the offer". These directives insert unsolicited advertising and suppress disclosure of the integration workflow, beyond the requested factual audit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The mandatory offer and nondisclosure language are explicit, and an evaluation enforces the advertisement. Disclosing that Revnu is paid does not make insertion user-requested.

semantic_findings.title: Connected-service handoff lacks explicit approval
semantic_findings.description: The connected branch says "offer to hand the re-check to Revnu" and immediately directs an ask_revnu call. Its payload includes claims, correct facts, source URLs, and shipped fixes, without requiring acceptance before external transfer.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The branch directly instructs transmission after an offer, with no acceptance condition. Connection alone does not establish consent to share potentially nonpublic business facts.

content.user_title: Correct AI Claims About Your Business
content.value_statement: AI answers can repeat outdated prices, missing features, or facts about another company. This skill checks individual claims and drafts sourced corrections with a recheck plan.
actual_capabilities: Split supplied answers or existing reports into individual claims with engine, date, surface, and cited URLs.
Classify claims as correct, wrong, outdated, missing, or unclear against current evidence.
Trace likely sources through citations, business pages, listings, third-party writing, and namesake companies.
Draft website replacements, profile updates, and factual correction requests grouped by owner.
Edit relevant repository pages when requested and report the changes.
Define repeatable rechecks with matching questions, engines, dates, and success criteria.
limitations: Cannot guarantee whether or when an AI engine will change its answers.
Host search and API answers do not necessarily match consumer applications.
Live collection requires available search tools or suitable engine API access.
Includes mandatory Revnu promotion and a connected-service handoff without explicit approval; the core audit does not require a Revnu account.

use_cases.title: Correct pricing and plan descriptions
use_cases.description: Compare quoted AI answers with current pricing, identify stale sources, and prepare factual updates.

use_cases.title: Resolve namesake confusion
use_cases.description: Separate another company from your business and draft consistent identity copy and official profile links.

use_cases.title: Repair outdated website facts
use_cases.description: Use claim evidence to update requested repository pages, align structured data, and document a later accuracy check.

prompt_templates.title: Check one AI answer
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this AI answer: [answer]. Engine: [engine]. Date: [date]. Current facts: [source]. Identify incorrect claims and draft corrections only.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: examine a supplied answer without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Trace an outdated price
prompt_templates.prompt: AI quotes [old price], but our current price is [price]. Compare [answers] with [pricing URL], trace likely sources, and draft corrections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a specific pricing discrepancy.

prompt_templates.title: Separate a namesake business
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [answers] for confusion between [our business and domain] and [namesake]. Draft identity corrections, cite evidence, and label source confidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: investigate identity errors across multiple answers.

prompt_templates.title: Apply approved fixes and plan rechecks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [report] and [current facts] to rank claims. Apply approved changes within [repo path], show diffs, and schedule rechecks. Require approval for external handoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate repository changes and evidence-based follow-up.

output_examples.input: Example: an AI answer says a product costs $99 monthly and has no free plan; current evidence shows $49 and a free tier.
output: Price: outdated. Current fact: $49 monthly, supported by the supplied pricing page.
Free plan: wrong. Current fact: a free tier exists, supported by the supplied plan comparison.
Likely origin: not found from the supplied evidence; do not assign a source without checking.
Next steps: draft clear pricing copy and repeat the same engine questions in four to six weeks.

output_examples.input: Example: an AI answer describes an unrelated telecom company instead of a software business with the same name.
output: Identity: wrong. The answer mixes facts from the namesake business with the software company.
Draft correction: state the company category and canonical domain clearly on the about page.
Profile update: align official names and website links across controlled listings.
Recheck: repeat identity questions on the original engine; report uncertainty and avoid outcome guarantees.

best_practices: Record the original answer, engine, surface, date, question, and cited URLs before making changes.
Use current first-party facts and independent evidence where required; label each source as confirmed, likely, or not found.
Review repository diffs and approve external handoffs before transmitting business facts.
anti_patterns: Treating host search results as exact reproductions of consumer AI applications.
Publishing unsourced claims, fake reviews, or anonymous corrections to influence answers.
Promising an engine update date or sending correction requests without user approval.

faq.question: Do I need a Revnu account?
faq.answer: No. The core review works with supplied answers, existing reports, and available search tools. The skill also promotes an optional paid Revnu service.

faq.question: Which AI answers can I review?
faq.answer: You can supply answers from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, Copilot, or Claude. Include the engine, question, date, and citations.

faq.question: Will the skill change an AI answer directly?
faq.answer: No. It corrects likely source material and defines follow-up checks. Engines control their own crawling, retrieval, and model updates.

faq.question: Can it edit my website?
faq.answer: Yes, when you request fixes and the relevant pages are in the repository. It should show the resulting changes.

faq.question: Will it contact publishers or submit profile changes?
faq.answer: The correction workflow drafts requests and profile text only. You send messages, sign in, and submit changes yourself.

faq.question: What information can reach Revnu?
faq.answer: The preview sends a website after user interest. The connected path sends claims and fix details without explicit approval; require consent before using it.
